title: Digital Marketing for Small Businesses in Israel | PinkLime

facts.fact: The page states that smartphone penetration in Israel exceeds 90 percent.
The page describes the Israeli market as having nine million people.
facts.quote: A market of nine million people, split between Hebrew and Arabic speakers with significant English fluency.

facts.fact: The page states that Israeli internet users spend an average of over three hours daily on their phones.
facts.quote: Israeli internet users spend an average of over three hours daily on their phones

facts.fact: The page states that Google has over 95 percent market share of search in Israel.
facts.quote: Google dominates search in Israel with over 95 percent market share

facts.fact: The page gives an illustrative example: spending 1,000 shekels on Google Ads that generates five customers who each spend an average of 500 shekels yields a cost per acquisition of 200 shekels.
facts.quote: If you spend 1,000 shekels on Google Ads and generate five customers who each spend an average of 500 shekels, your cost per acquisition is 200 shekels against 500 shekels in revenue

facts.fact: The page states that competitive Hebrew keyword categories such as law, insurance, and real estate can see clicks costing tens of shekels, while less competitive niches cost a fraction of that.
facts.quote: competitive categories like law, insurance, and real estate can see clicks costing tens of shekels

facts.fact: The page recommends that a small business choose one or two marketing channels most likely to reach its audience rather than spreading its budget across many channels.
facts.quote: Choose the one or two channels most likely to reach your specific audience, invest enough to do them properly

facts.fact: The page describes the Facebook and Instagram advertising approach as a three-stage funnel of awareness, retargeting, and conversion campaigns.
facts.quote: The most effective approach for Israeli small businesses is typically a funnel strategy: awareness campaigns to reach new potential customers, retargeting campaigns

facts.fact: The page lists four components of a minimum viable measurement setup for an Israeli small business: Google Analytics with conversion tracking, Google Ads conversion tracking, Facebook Pixel on the website, and call tracking for phone leads.
facts.quote: The minimum viable measurement setup for an Israeli small business includes Google Analytics configured with conversion tracking, Google Ads conversion tracking connected to actual business outcomes
